Short answer: what does the law require before a Uruguayan wine label can name a place?
A certificate from the competent body, INAVI (Decree 283/993, article 15)
The grapes must be grown in that area (article 17)
The producer is entered in INAVI's register of geographical indications (article 16; Law 17.011, articles 76–77)

Under Decree 283/993 a label naming a geographical indication needs a certificate of the right to use it from the competent body, the producer must be in INAVI's register of geographical indications of origin, and the grapes must come from that area. Law 17.011 confirms that INAVI is the competent body for national wine.
Short answer: why do we say Uruguay's vineyards are concentrated in the south? Use figures.
Canelones has 66.77% of the national area
The three Metropolitana departments together hold about 83%

On INAVI's 2025 report Canelones alone has 66.77% of the national area, and with Montevideo and San José the three Metropolitana departments hold about 83%. Northern departments such as Salto, Paysandú and Rivera each have under 2%.
